title: DOM order of blocks
evidence: Block DOM order follows the phone layout rows, top to bottom, then left to right: 8 of 8 demo sections and 265 of 304 corpus sections with 2+ blocks (desktop row order: 173). The 39 exceptions are not explained, because live capture can't read them. They are not out of scope. Live on a probe page (parity/findings/CAP-ORDER.json): DOM order followed the phone row order in every read, after moves on desktop and on phones. Built: after an edit, the section whose blocks changed takes that order, in the model and in the DOM; a saved page stays as it loads, a section next door stays, and undo brings the order back (headless Chrome, npm run mid-check). Ours, not measured on the oracle: blocks with the same z paint in DOM order, and moving one flipped the paint in our editor, so a pair that overlaps with the same z, on desktop or on the phone, keeps its order. Those pairs never swap, the rest follow the phone rows, and a chain of three stays in order. elementFromPoint reads the same block on top before and after an edit. In such a section DOM order can differ from the phone rows: the corpus has 7 such pairs in 4 sections, and in none does the phone order want a flip. Run: add, duplicate, Move Forward and Backward, stack, copy and paste, and unstack leave no new overlapping pair with the same z, so such a pair comes from a loaded page. Read in the code, not run: the layers panel drag and a group's Move Forward, which only renumber. Not checked: paint where a block's content runs outside its box onto a neighbour with the same z. A desktop edit and the phone: read on the probe page (parity/findings/CAP-DESKMOVE.json to CAP-DESKMOVE9.json, with CAP-ORDER.json), and built for sections made here with Add Blank (npm run neworder-check, with the mouse and keys, which also reads the rows the phone draws). Any desktop move or resize, of one block or a group, by mouse or arrow key, and a text block that grows when typed in, sets the phone order again, and a new block goes through the same rule, coming last in the old stack. A smaller block with at least 80% of its area inside a bigger one (75% does not, 80% does, by columns and by rows) belongs to the first of the smallest blocks that hold it, and comes right after that block with the others it holds. Blocks taken in that order, top first, then left first, each go after the last block they share columns with, and past blocks to their left that they share none with. If the old stack starts at phone row 1 with a block one row high, the order turns so that block lands last: it goes last, then first on the next edit, whichever block was edited. Each block keeps its phone height and the gap above it. A copy on desktop (Cmd+D) goes last on the phone and takes its source's z + 1, even if another block has that z (7 of 7 fresh). A paste takes its source's z + 1 too (3 reads). A block taken away, on either width, moves the blocks below up by its height, but no higher than where it started; gaps above them stay. A phone whose start was moved by hand, or with blocks that overlap after a phone resize, stops following the desktop. A new block on a stopped phone takes the older size rule. #186's rule that a moved Line goes after the blocks it shares columns with was wrong: moving isn't the trigger and neither is being a Line, a Shape cut to one phone row does it too, and a Line made two rows does not.
